transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-29    Time: 15:00 UTC    Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Suarez (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Redwood SE) — Liam O'Connor (Zenith Head of ML), Sofia Alvarez (Zenith Platform), Rajesh Kumar (CFO)

[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR. quick agenda — usage & cost, reliability/latency, roadmap, and then next steps. liam, do you want to kick off with how things are looking on your side?
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: yeah thanks ava. overall things are good, Q4 usage ramped up — roughly 2.6x compared to Q3, mostly around new algo rollout for our risk scoring. cost is up, obviously, tokens spiked during market open windows, um, and we wanted to understand options — like d e d i c a t e d capacity vs hosted, and where we can optimize.
[00:35] Diego Suarez: totally. we pulled some initial numbers ahead of this call, and the spike looks concentrated in that 09:30 to 09:45 UTC window, plus some longer prompt chains from the new scoring pipeline. i can share the token-level sheet after the call.
[00:48] Sofia Alvarez: one thing — we saw occasional 99th percentile latency jumps to 1.2s per token which is causing downstream timeouts in our feed. it's intermittent but consistent enough to surface.
[01:02] Maya Patel: thanks, that matches what we saw in the telemetry. a couple immediate things — batching strategy and KV cache warmup are big levers. we noticed your sequence lengths vary a lot; some bursts create inefficient batching. we can propose config tweaks and also test a dedicated pool with pinned GPUs to remove noisy neighbor effects.
[01:25] Rajesh Kumar: from finance point of view i need clarity on unit economics. how much can committed capacity save us versus pay-as-you-go hosted? and what's the minimum commitment?
[01:38] Ava Chen: great Qs. quick overview — hosted gives simple unit pricing but can be more expensive at peak. dedicated (reserved) offers predictable throughput and discounts — typical commitments range monthly to annual; we'll send tiered options. we also have autoscale burst options to handle spikes.
[01:55] Liam O'Connor: can you remind us on the data residency and encryption guarantees? we have some new compliance checks for european clients.
[02:03] Diego Suarez: yes — SOC2 plus customer-controlled keys via KMS for private deployments, and VPC options. we'll share the SOC2 and KMS integration docs. note: in our private deployment offering we can also do on-prem for air-gapped needs, but that's typically a separate enterprise engagement.
[02:22] Sofia Alvarez: would Dedicated still let us keep the KV cache warm between requests? that's critical for latency.
[02:28] Maya Patel: yes, dedicated pools are exactly for that — pinned workers and warm KV caches. also we can tune the cache eviction policies based on your prompt prefixes. small caveat: if you want super low cold-start for infrequent routes, there are tradeoffs with cost.
[02:46] Liam O'Connor: on the perf side, i'd like the SE team to run an end-to-end benchmark using our actual prompt set and peak traffic. is that doable?
[02:53] Maya Patel: absolutely — if you can share the prompt set and a sample trace of traffic, we can reproduce the spike and run dedicated vs hosted comparisons. note: there may be minor differences in reported latency due to network egress, but we'll keep instrumentation consistent.
[03:12] Rajesh Kumar: what about reliability SLA? we need to ensure 99.9 uptime and clear escalation paths for trading hours.
[03:20] Ava Chen: for Dedicated we provide SLA-backed uptime and a dedicated support path; for hosted we have incident SLAs based on plan. Diego will follow up with the SLA doc and escalation contacts.
[03:33] Liam O'Connor: any quick wins on cost? beyond dedicated — like quantization or batching changes?
[03:39] Maya Patel: yes — a few items: 1) prompt engineering to reduce average token length (we can run a prompt audit), 2) dynamic batching windows to match your latency SLOs, 3) recommending a quantized model variant for scores with similar quality but ~20-30% token-cost savings. we'll include a quality / regression check in the benchmark.
[03:59] Sofia Alvarez: quick flag — some of our infra team called out if we moved to Dedicated, what's the rollout complexity? network, VPC peering, KMS, etc.
[04:09] Diego Suarez: we've done Dedicated onboarding with a standard checklist — VPC setup, KMS key exchange, SSO (SAML) config, and test deploy. typically 2–4 weeks depending on approvals.
[04:22] Liam O'Connor: okay great. can you also include an estimate for cost during the onboarding month (since we'll run both hosted and dedicated in parallel briefly)?
[04:30] Ava Chen: yes we'll model a hybrid month and show incremental costs.
[04:34] [Short silence / crosstalk]
[04:40] Maya Patel: small note — some terms in telemetry looked like 'KV cache' were transcribed as K V cash in our notes, so apologies for any confusion.
[04:48] Liam O'Connor: haha yeah i've seen that too.
[04:51] Ava Chen: ok let's summarize recs and next steps. Diego — share the Q4 token usage CSV and the SOC2 + security links; Maya — run the 99th-pct latency benchmark on both hosted and a proposed Dedicated config once liam uploads the prompt set; i'll draft a committed capacity pricing sheet with a couple of term options for rajesh.
[05:10] Rajesh Kumar: timeline? we're looking to finalize contract by mid-January to align with budgeting.
[05:16] Ava Chen: got it — target follow-up week of Jan 4th. Diego will send the data request, maya will run benchmarks asap, and we'll reconvene to go over results and pricing.
[05:28] Liam O'Connor: sounds good. one final Q — competitors: we did a small eval with h f self-hosted and anthropic last quarter, any notes on migration complexity?
[05:38] Maya Patel: self-hosting adds ops lift for kernel selection, packing, and GPU tuning; Redwood's value is the runtime and ops controls plus observability — we can outline the delta in the benchmark doc.
[05:50] Ava Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[05:54] Diego Suarez: thanks, i'll send the deck and sheet; expect an email by EOD tomorrow.
[05:58] Sofia Alvarez: thank you all.
[06:00] Call ended.
